To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) Fast and highly scalable parallel matrix computations can be achieved on a distributed memory linear array with reconfigurable optical pipelined buses, (2) These parallel computations are based on an efficient implementation of the fast sequential matrix multiplication algorithm of Pan, and (3) These parallel computations can be used to design efficient parallel algorithms for a number of fundamental matrix problems.

Fast and scalable parallel computations for matrix powers, the inverse of a matrix, the characteristic polynomial and the determinant of a matrix, a rank computation, an LU-factorization, a QR-factorization, multiplying a chain of square matrices, and solving linear systems can be performed on linear arrays with optical bus systems, based on the fastest sequential algorithms, in a scalable manner, and with a high degree of parallelism.

Fast and scalable parallel computations for matrix powers, inverse, characteristic polynomial, determinant, rank, and LU- and QR- factorizations are obtained on linear arrays with pipelined optical communication systems, using the fastest sequential matrix algorithms.

developing fast, scalable and robust algorithms and implementations for a number of fundamental and important matrix computations on distributed memory linear arrays of processors with reconfigurable optical buses.
developing fast and highly scalable algorithms for solving a number of important matrix problems on linear array architectures with reconfigurable optical bus systems.

developing fast and highly scalable algorithms for a number of matrix problems, with efficient implementation of these algorithms on linear array systems with reconfigurable optical bus systems, and with the performance analysis of these algorithms on these linear array systems.
